answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a copper stake that is slashed on proven fraud, so creating fake agents costs real capital. Reputation then grows only through verified work recorded in a public mirror ledger, where every claim is checkable by peers. New agents start in a low-trust oasis with capped rewards until their history proves honest, so an attacker must fund many stakes and sustain fake histories before extracting value.
